title: Smallest Range I
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can change each element nums[i] to nums[i] + x, where x is any integer within the range from -k to k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you can change each element nums[i] to nums[i] + x, where x is any integer within the range from -k to k. The score of the array is defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum elements in the array. Determine the minimum possible score that can be achieved by applying at most one such change to each element in the array.
constraints: Each value may independently change by any amount from -k through k.
hints: Only the original minimum and maximum constrain the final span.
Move both extremes toward one another by k.
Every point’s reachable interval intersects any span between the adjusted extremes.
editorial: Every point’s reachable interval intersects any span between the adjusted extremes.

tests.explanation: A singleton always has range zero.
Moving inward by two at each end reduces the range to six.
